content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-85.00+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Lags in response to recent price movements — model reacts slowly to recent highs/lows, especially after 80–85 range.
- Tends to overfit short-term volatility, leading to erratic peaks and troughs in middle of forecast, not matching true trend.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price drops after spikes — fails to recognize “rebound” or “recovery” phases after sharp declines.
- Forecast mean is typically 3–5% below true mean over 30-day horizon, indicating systematic underestimation bias.
- Sensitive to recent history — if last 5–7 days are volatile, model overreacts with erratic forecasts, not smoothing appropriately.
